name: Signal Origins: The BCI Rollout and the People Who Said No
description: A carefully licensed but genuinely critical historical documentary tracing the mandatory BCI rollout of 2091-2155 through the experiences of refusers, the legal frameworks used to compel compliance, and the fates of communities that resisted integration. Director Priyanka Volkov-Adeyemi spent eight years interviewing the elderly survivors of pre-BCI communities and their descendants, producing a film that is scrupulously factual and quietly devastating. The holographic format was a deliberate choice — the director noted that making a film about people who refused neural technology in the most invasive immersive format was intentional provocation.
cultural_impact: The film revitalized the Unclocked movement and is credited with doubling membership in BCI-refuser communities within two years of release.
story_hooks: One of the film's interview subjects — a 94-year-old woman who successfully evaded BCI implantation for her entire life — is found dead the week the film wins a major distribution prize.
The denied HelixCorp content challenge contains internal memos that, if leaked, would expose the corporation's ongoing efforts to retroactively rewrite BCI consent documentation.
A Tier 2 viewer who watches the holographic version experiences an unexplained feedback loop in their BCI during the refuser testimony sequences — and they're not the only one.
